correctness.rationale: For a connected graph \(H\) of order at least three, any independent set in its central graph contains a clique \(X\) of original vertices and only subdivision vertices coming from edges of \(H-X\). Connectivity and the clique property imply that at least \(|X|\) edges of \(H\) are incident with \(X\), hence \(|X|+|E(H-X)|\le |E(H)|\); all subdivision vertices attain equality, proving \(lpha(C(H))=|E(H)|\). Substituting this identity together with the exact order/size formulas for a central graph into the cited second-iterate formula simplifies algebraically to \(i(C^k(G))=2|E(C^{k-2}(G))|\); the \(K_2,k=3\) boundary case is checked separately.

broader_coverage.reasoning: That result does not by itself remove dependence on \(lpha(H)\) at all subsequent iterates; the audited lemma supplies the collapsing substitution.
